takeaways: Nomad's $532/kWh equipment price sits between BNEF's US turnkey ($219, 4-h, 100 MW class) and the disclosed utility-owned projects ($513-584). For a 12-unit, 2-h, FEOC-era order in New England that is a fair price.
is above every national all-in index because those indices are four-hour and 60-150 MW. NREL's own cost structure (pack $/kWh x hours + BOS $/kW) puts a 2-h system at roughly 1.3-1.5x the 4-h $/kWh.

is not a battery benchmark at all. It carries a switching station, feeder protection at Station 496, a landfill platform, Article 80 siting, indirects and AFUDC. The closest published analogue is Provincetown at $1,289/kWh (2022 dollars, no separate station, existing site).
No published index includes a utility's indirects or AFUDC.
Strip J-M and Hyde Park is $1,483/kWh direct; strip the station and site layers D and E as well and it is $1,156/kWh.
